explanation: The English article on the Gulf war traces the invasion of Kuwait to what the earlier war left behind. By the time Iraq signed the ceasefire with Iran in August 1988 it was deep in debt, most of it owed to Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, and the debts to Kuwait alone came to fourteen billion dollars. Iraq pressed both states to forgive them and both refused. The article adds that Kuwait was overproducing oil, at least in part to repair losses Iranian attacks had caused during the war, and that the slump in the price that followed cost Iraq seven billion dollars a year. That is the grievance the Iraqi government described as economic warfare.
